subject: Hosted Trial: quickstart plan, endpoint mapping & traffic profile
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@novaretail.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted Trial: quickstart plan, endpoint mapping & traffic profile

Alex — great to meet today, thanks for the demo time. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we can get your hosted trial started: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use: conversational product search & personalization (low single-digit second latency target)
- Peak traffic: expected 90–120 requests/sec during morning batch, baseline ~12 req/s off-peak
- Outputs: short generated responses (avg 120 tokens), and periodic embeddings for indexing

Our proposed Hosted quickstart (what we can provision immediately)
1) Sandbox endpoints: 2 endpoints — gen-primary (for UIs) and emb-index (for embeddings)
2) Default rate guards: 200 rps total burst-cap; steady-state throttle to match your profile (we'll dial after traffic sample)
3) KV/prefix caching enabled on gen-primary to reduce token cost for common queries
4) Short canary (48–72h) to validate latency and cost on your real traffic

Next actions
- Can you send a 48–72h traffic sample (timestamps + endpoint + avg tokens)? (we can accept csv)
- I'll loop in Ben for endpoint mapping and Priyom for SRE playbook and access steps
- We can produce a short SOW and sandbox access link once procurement confirms PO details

Attachments: Redwood quickstart one-pager attached.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_quickstart-onepager.pdf (PDF, 85KB)]
From: Alex Chen <alex@novaretail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@novaretail.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted Trial: quickstart plan, endpoint mapping & traffic profile

Sean — thanks, this aligns with how we described things internally. Attached is a 72-hour slice from last week (trimmed, anonymized): nova_traffic_sample_Q3.csv. It has request timestamps, endpoint (search_gen / embeddings), avg_input_tokens, avg_output_tokens.

A couple clarifications: 
- We expect embeddings to be batched every ~30s from a background job (so spikes are brief)
- We do need <200ms P99 for cached, and <600ms P95 for cold gen requests if possible (desktop users).

Procurement looped in for PO process. Can you confirm whether the sandbox endpoints will be in us-west region? Also fine to start with Hosted — we only want to discuss Dedicated if latency/cost doesn't meet our SLOs after the trial.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Product - Search | NovaRetail
[attachment: nova_traffic_sample_Q3.csv (CSV, 14KB)]
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@novaretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, procure@novaretail.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted Trial: quickstart plan, endpoint mapping & traffic profile

Alex — received, thanks for the sample. Quick responses and a few asks so Ben & Priyom can size/provision correctly: 

Questions for sizing
- Is the 72h extract representative of a normal week or a promotional spike?
- Typical payload sizes for search_gen requests (text length) — avg input tokens looks right but any long-tail examples?
- For embeddings: preferred batching window (you said ~30s) and whether the background job can tolerate a 2–3s variance on the request side

Region & endpoints
- Sandbox will be provisioned in us-west initially (we can mirror to eu for later tests)

Proposed short timeline
- 48h: sandbox endpoints + access, smoke tests with your QA
- 48–72h run: live traffic to validate latency and cost (we'll eyeball P95/P99)
- Close + next: hand off to procurement for short SOW/PO or discuss moving to Dedicated if SLOs not met

Ben & Priyom — any additional prep (network allowlists, token rotation, team access)?

Sean
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@novaretail.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, procure@novaretail.com
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted Trial: quickstart plan, endpoint mapping & traffic profile

Alex — quick tech notes from infra: 
- Endpoints & rate limits: we'll create two endpoint IDs (search_gen, emb_index). Default soft-limit: 250 rps with 1s token-bucket burst. We can mutate that per your traffic shape after the first 24h.
- Cache behavior: prefix caching for search_gen (configurable TTL). For your <200ms cached P99 requirement, we'll prioritize routing to cached responses when key hits occur.
- Network/setup asks: please supply the IP ranges for your QA runners and the service account email for token provisioning (we'll provide RBAC instructions).
- Observability: we'll share a sandbox dashboard link with token-level latency and token-cost breakdowns.

If you want, Priyom and I can run a 30–45m technical preflight tomorrow to walk through the CSV and confirm mapping rules.

Ben Carter
SRE & Deployments | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <alex@novaretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@novaretail.com, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@novaretail.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted Trial: quickstart plan, endpoint mapping & traffic profile

Thanks all — this looks good. Procurement (procure@novaretail.com) will coordinate PO and needs the short SOW and billing contact. Jordan (cc'd) will own integration work on our side. 

We confirm: 
- Proceed with Hosted sandbox in us-west.
- We'll provide IP ranges and service account this afternoon.
- We'll run the smoke tests from QA and report results; if latency misses our targets we'll discuss Dedicated sizing, but start with Hosted as proposed.

Requested by procurement: please send a 1-page SOW with trial duration, estimated token budget, and acceptance criteria (latency P95/P99 thresholds). Also include a contact for billing.

I'll follow up once procure has the PO cadence. Looking forward to the preflight — Alex
